content: Ranunculales is an order of flowering plants. This order necessarily includes the family Ranunculaceae, commonly known as the buttercup family. Both the APG system (1998) and the APG II system (2003) recognize Ranunculales as a distinct order and classify it among the basal eudicots, without assigning it to a more specific clade. The term optional segregate family refers to families that may be split off from the preceding family under certain taxonomic interpretations. Under this definition, well-known members of the Ranunculales order include buttercups, clematis, columbines, delphiniums, and poppies. The Cronquist system (1981) also recognized Ranunculales as an order but placed it within the subclass Magnoliidae, which is part of the class Magnoliopsida. The Cronquist system defined the order Ranunculales to include the following families: Ranunculaceae, Circaeasteraceae, Berberidaceae, Sargentodoxaceae, Lardizabalaceae, Menispermaceae, Coriariaceae, and Sabiaceae. In the Cronquist system, the families Papaveraceae and Fumariaceae (including plants in the optional family Pteridophyllaceae) were treated as part of a separate order called Papaverales. This order was also placed within the same subclass, Magnoliidae.
